utterances.text: Leader, commander. But not -- not -- not military commander. Leader, the lead, Mr. Hadzic, the big guy. I -- I said that earlier, I think, in this court, that we've never been introduced officially with -- with -- with his title or rank and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you can't recall anyone ever having told you a specific position that he held; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, the police were saying that he is in charge of the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, with respect, sir, that's not a position.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So I'm asking you, can you recall whether anyone -- whether you have any information given to you at the time as to what position he held?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ever hear him referred to as a doctor?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You see, sir, I am very puzzled by your testimony --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- because Mr. Lubin did come here and testify about his meetings with Mr. -- with a Hadzic, but he testified categorically that the person he met --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is completely against the guide-lines, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But Mr. President -- well, maybe I misunderstand the guide-lines because I'm not going to ask this witness to comment on his credibility, but I am, I believe - and I may be wrong, I may be misunderstanding the guide-lines - but I thought that I would be permitted to indicate that there is someone who was present who contradicts this witness's testimony. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm looking at guide-line 24 which says that a cross-examining party may put to a witness the evidence obtained from a previous witness provided that the identity of that witness is not given. And as my learned friend says it, parties are not asked -- are not to ask witnesses to comment on credibility but this is not the focus. The focus is the identify of that witness. The damage has been done now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But, Mr. President, Mr. Lubin was not a protected witness, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's not -- that's not the point, Mr. Gosnell. The guide-line is about two different things: (a) mentioning the identity of a previous witness; and (b), questioning the witness on the stand about the credibility of the previous witness. So there is a (a) and a (b) --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But, Mr. President, I'm not proposing to do either of those. All I wish to do is to put the evidence to the witness that has been heard by Your Honours, and I think the only fair way for this witness to respond or to answer is for him to, indeed, know the source of the evidence. But I'm in Your Honours' hands. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, actually, you're out of my hands, Mr. Gosnell, because the damage has been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, in -- in -- in your own jurisdiction, would you be allowed to put a question like that to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I -- I believe I would. But I -- I may be wrong. But I believe that I would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Abd El Razek, let me ask you this: Did you ever speak with Mr. Lubin about the identity of the person with whom you were meeting -- that you met on this occasion four days before the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We all discussed the upcoming meeting with Mr. Hadzic, including the sector commander, Mr. Lubin, and Mr. Zitterman the civil police in charge. We often discussed what's going on -- actually, it was our business, our day, and half night business because during night-time we were not allowed to meet, but our day business was to talk about what was going on on the territory in those area, who is who, who is doing what, when, and what's happening. We are a team -- or we were a team to discuss those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Mr. Lubin say that he believed that the person that you you were meeting was Dr. Mladen Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did he tell you that the person you were meeting was part of the local municipal Erdut authorities?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Hadzic was not local municipal that we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that you slept every night during those ten days while you were in Sector East in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sleeping is one thing and staying overnight there is something else. We hardly slept. But we were under curfew, and we -- every evening we would go to that place. We rushed to see if we can still have a warm water before the electricity will take off, and we'll sit there chatting, doing whatever we could do, coffee or tea on -- on gas oven, not on electric oven, and spend the night. And early in morning we were happy to leave because our headquarter was more warmer and the heat was properly working than our apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you had to stay put in your location after night-fall because there was a curfew in place.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you couldn't move around during that curfew; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Except -- except when we were invited to go to the JNA boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm going to come back to that occasion.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But it's right to say, then, that from dusk until dawn every night during those ten days you stayed in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How many times, if you can recall, did you visit the Baranja region?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beli Manastir? Sir? The Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Beli Manastir or the other towns in -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Beli Manastir was my focus on visiting outside Erdut. Dalj also, or Dalj, call it, was target for visiting. We did Vukovar visit just for familiarity and -- and -- and to see the remains of Vukovar. I believe I went to Beli Manastir three times. One time coming back, we stopped at some of a small town, that we had coffee. In Dalj we visited our civil police and the UNMO. And any time we go to Osijek, and I went hardly twice, we'll pass through Dalj, see the -- our folks, and will continue to co-ordinate with the UNMOs so we can cross the mine line crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And am I right that you believed that there was a Belgian UNPROFOR battalion based in the town where you were staying which you say is Erdut?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Was no battalion. Was the sector commander was a Belgian and the battalion was stationed in Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we turn back to page 3 of the document on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Paragraph 11: "There was a Belgian UNPROFOR battalion based in Erdut, which was joined by a Russian UNPROFOR platoon of around 30 soldiers one week after our arrival."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. With all due respect, when we went through this, I re-corrected, I re -- I asked my investigator, the Prosecutor, to change this, to correct this. It's not a battalion. And I did that before coming to this respected court. It was some misunderstanding. The chief, the commander of the sector was not the commander of the battalion. The commander of the battalion was Mr. Joachim, who was stationed in Beli Manastir. We had -- when we came, we had hardly seven military personnel from UNPROFOR, and then we had something, 20 to 30, young Russian soldiers coming the week after I arrived. The battalion itself was stationed, and after I left, still there, Belgian battalion commanded by Colonel Joachim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And Lieutenant-Colonel Joachim was based in Beli Manastir; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Paragraph 13: "In Erdut we would confer daily together with Lubin, the Belgian battalion commander, and myself" --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is incorrect. It's not Belgian battalion. It's a Belgian sector commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is there any possibility at all that you're confused about the town that you were in for at least some of your time in Sector East?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not. I -- I talked to my colleagues or your colleagues in -- in -- in this respected organisation, that this is a mistake. And maybe also my mistake, that I saw that, I sign it, I skipped my mind to see Belgian battalion commander. Joachim never lived in Erdut. The one who lived in Erdut was the sector commander, Belgians, higher rank, I think lieutenant-general or general, full general. Not lieutenant -- not Colonel Joachim. This I -- I -- I firmly insist on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, do you remember the name of that sector commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wrote it down, and I think I had a photo with -- with him, photo with his Chief of Staff, and I wrote on back of the photo his name. I handed those photos to Mr. Alex. And if ... it is in his hands --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We have the document, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do have it. We disclosed it to the Defence. We haven't added it to the 65 ter list, but if it is relevant we can make it available. I'm not sure if they're available in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's not really necessary. Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, how would you describe your facial hair?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My facial hair? In -- in Arabic we say Krmshi [phoen], Krmshi meaning it's brownish. I am the lightest in feature in my family. My brothers are darker than myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, I wasn't specific enough. I didn't mean the colour.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I was interested in how you groom your face. How would you describe that, your facial hair?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I like myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- I -- it's very attractive on you, sir --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But I'm wondering what word you would use in English --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For my face?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- to describe your facial hair? Aside from an adjective or description, how would you describe how you wear your facial hair?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My moustache. Many people confuse in United States with Latinos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, Mr. Abd El Razek, my friend sitting next to me, how would you describe his facial hair?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I, sir? Can I?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, what word would you use? And there's no need for too many adjectives. We're looking for a noun, sir.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very respected face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, I think Mr. Gosnell is trying to get the difference between what you call a moustache --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Moustache and beard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a bearded face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: There you are, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that the man sitting at the back --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Not the man immediately behind me, the man sitting at the back, is he also wearing a beard?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hadzic, always, nice beard. It used to be darker. And moustache, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember that you had a telephone conversation with an investigator or -- and perhaps a lawyer in 2012? Do you remember that, first of all?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Telephone what? He called me home in Jerusalem to invite me to the meeting, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In June 2012 do you remember that you had a conversation with Mr. Demirdjian and Mr. Versonnen?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- I came to this city quarter to be investigated. It starts June? I think so, maybe. June. Is it June?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent two days with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps this would be before you were speaking to them face to face. Was there occasion or perhaps after or in between, do you remember having a telephone conversation with some people from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I believe Roel called me to Jerusalem. I think that then -- then maybe Alex did. Some logistic people, trafficking people, the ticket people. I received two, three calls to Jerusalem from the city quarter to facilitate my arrival to this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 1D518, please, which is Defence tab 301.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In any event, am I right in saying that during the telephone conversation, you weren't able to look at any photographs. They didn't send you a fax with a photograph during the time of that conversation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No photos. Of course, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you seen this document that's now on the screen during the course of this last weekend when you were preparing for your testimony? Did you have a look at this.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I read this thing. I seen that first -- the first page on a -- the title, yes. But ... but not the details of page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You didn't read this during the course of the weekend?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe something down the pages. If you go down, I may refresh my mind. That's all? One page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, this is a one-page document, sir.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, leaving aside whether you saw this document, now that you've looked at it, do you recall that you had a telephone conversation in which you mentioned these facts to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- if you mean the description of Mr. Hadzic, I did emphasise the moustache, not the beard. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, why wouldn't you say beard if, as we've already established you understand beard to be precisely how Mr. Hadzic's facial hair is groomed?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said moustache. I emphasised the moustache, not the beard. You understand what I'm saying. They asked if I can describe the man. I said tall, dark, with moustache, and maybe I skipped to say beard. But I -- then my correction, impression that he was tall, like I said also handsome. It's not here -- written here. Pleasant face with moustache. I did not describe [indiscernible]. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it's correct that during the conversation you did not describe him as having a beard; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's, I think, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And why wouldn't you simply say he had a beard?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It skipped my mind. I mean, you go to the human mind and ask why you -- you -- you know -- you're familiar with the Gestalt test, you know, I -- the first impression, the beard or the moustache or the eyes or the eyeglasses. Many of my colleagues who did work on their nose the first thing that they were asked they did something with their eyes or glasses. I -- this is images that I don't know how -- you don't have control on those things and I'm not saying that it is correct or it is objectively right. This is human impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please have 4924.5, which is a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you see this picture during the weekend before you came to testify?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you remember how it was shown to you? What were the circumstances? What was said about this photograph when it was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that I'm going to see pictures, movies, silent, and I was asked if I can recognise some of those people. It is what were at least believed four or five photos. I was not led to those personalities. I was told please let us know if you can recognise -- whom you can recognise, and, to tell you the truth, I immediately recognised Mr. Hadzic in the four, five photos that I was seeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you immediately recognise him in this frame, in this video?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, to me, that's a very fuzzy image. I'd like to know how, after, 22 years, 21 years, you could have instantly picked out that man as being Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did with Mladic, I did it with Karadzic. I did with other people that I recognised. I told this respected court last day that I have problems with names but I can visualise things for 20, 30 years. As -- it's something that I have it from God. Maybe from the parents' genes. But this is me. And with the names, it's difficult. Places, yes, I can recognise very well. Faces, I recognise and remember very well. Sometimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, let me just intercede here. And one of the people that you recognised on this videos was Milan Gvero; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How many times did you meet Mr., or General Gvero?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice at least. Twice or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So we please have 4845.1. And for this, I'll need the Prosecutor's kind assistance. And it's 50 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Or we can just stop it there.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, I tell you something. This is Mladic for sure. Hadzic for sure. For Gvero, I think this is a bit different. The nose is not Gvero nose. But it looks like Milan Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps we can move forward to the better image, which is 50 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that Gvero there to the left of Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought this morning. I said maybe it's Gvero. I did say this morning that I think it's Mr. Gvero. Now I re-look at him, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You have doubts now?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Because of the nose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Ever heard of someone named General Momir Talic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that that is General Momir Talic and it's not Milan Gvero.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I have my doubts too on my recollection. I'm not perfect, and I think that, you know, immediately I recognised my mistake with the nose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm done with that. Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. If we could have 1D518 back on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Again, this is a document we were just looking at. And, sir, I don't represent to you that this is your statement. This is a memo provided to us by the Prosecution of the content of your conversations with them, just so you understand clearly. And it says there -- and this is the phone conversation memo, and it says: "The third person on this page is Dr. Mladen Hadzic and the witness stated he had never heard of him." Now that suggests to me that you had some photographs in front of you. But I may be wrong. Maybe you only had a list of names. Did you have a list of names or did you have --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... the first testimony I never had photos. The 19, 12, I never saw photos. I had only names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. I should have read the entire paragraph to you to make clear what it says. It says: "The witness was provided a copy of the decision on the appointment of presidents and vice-presidents. The third person on this page is Dr. Mladen Hadzic and the witness stated he had never heard of him." Do you remember looking at his name back in 2012 and telling the Prosecutor that you'd never heard of Dr. Mladen Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that, you know, there is confusion between the doctor and Mr. Hadzic that I know. I never met the other Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But here you -- it's recorded that not only had you never met the other Hadzic, you had never heard of the other Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently. Apparently I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that what told them in 2012?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I mean, I tell you something. I did the testimony, I sign it, I was given the testimony to read and maybe skip a few things, but at large the testimony reflects my testimony to the ... I was told, asked, actually, later on, in Jerusalem, they send me names, asked me if I can recognise some of those names. I replied to them, to the best of my knowledge, most of names I -- I never tackled or met or knew. I looked at my lists again. I have very short list of names or whatever were Beli Manastir and the local -- Erdut and the area. I never met beyond that or recall, discuss, or seen report beyond that other names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 1D498, please. Defence tab 288.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Paragraph 5, this is another proofing note, and it's again a memo from the Prosecution telling us what you said during the weekend.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This weekend?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And down at paragraph 5 is says: "In relation to the last paragraph of 28 June 2012 proofing note, the witness states that he now recalls that there was another Hadzic besides Goran Hadzic but he did not meet him. "

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now my question -- let me get to my question: Back in 2012, you had a list in front of you, which included Dr. Mladen Hadzic's name. And at that time, you told the Prosecution that you had never heard of him?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Then you come here, and this weekend, which is a year later, a year further away from the events --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- now you are able to recall this man. Can you help us understand how and why that would happen?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Gossips, Lubin. Sorry for mentioning that, but I was told by my colleagues, not in the headquarters, that Lubin came and made statements on the other -- other Hadzic. And that -- that after I had the list and saying I don't recognise any names on those lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying you heard something about the content of Mr. Lubin's testimony and --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let me just finish my question. And that that reminded you that you had met another Hadzic named Mladen?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not say I had met. I said the name. Not met.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's my mistake. It reminded you that you had heard --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- of another individual named Mladen Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And this is after I received the list from -- from the colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But even though you now recall that there was a Mladen Hadzic, you -- that does not change your recollection that it was Goran Hadzic you met and not Mladen Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct. Correct. I never met the other Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm done with that document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Am I right that Mr. Lubin prepared sitreps promptly after the meetings or the events that he records in his sitreps?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a small correction. He wrote reports. The sitreps written by the army. If it is said sitrep here it's a mistake. He's -- the sitrep is a situation report done by sector commander. We as civilians or civil affairs we wrote reports or mostly we helped the sector commander to write a sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Whatever they may be called, did he prepare them promptly after the events described to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ever see these reports?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them I helped drafting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05932, please, which is Defence tab 78.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, can you say the number again please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Certainly. 05932 which is also P1389.1351.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this appears to be a communication from James Lubin --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- to Cedric Thornberry. It says: Situation report --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 21 April. Does that remind you that, in fact, situation reports were sent?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Is the sector commander's signature here?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Third line down, sir.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Third line. The meeting was warmest -- this is what you said? Paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No, the third line down. I'm just asking you if this refreshes your memory that these reports were called situation reports.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm, the form looks like situation reports, right. Sitrep. But the report is from -- apparently from Jim Lubin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's read paragraph 1: "Because" -- And again, the date is for the record is the 21st of April, 1992, or 1992.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "Because of yesterday's mass expulsions (total is 128 verified by CIVPOL), a letter of protest is being sent to Dr. Hadzic, president of local authorities Erdut. A copy of the Jovic letter will also be attached."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the confusion here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know, from your recollection, on the 19th or 20th or any days leading up to this date, was Mr. Lubin having separate meetings with -- with -- let me -- let me just complete my question -- was he having separate meetings with this Dr. Hadzic, who we understand whose first name is Mladen?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can testify that Mr. Lubin did have separate meetings with people as -- as I did myself too. We, in certain meetings we would go together. Certain other, each one go to run the meetings. I don't recall this name at all, Dr. Hadzic. And this report was written after I left, on the morning I left, so I do not have any clue of the content of this report at the time it was sent. Maybe later on I was seen -- shown by the colleague here. But, I, at the time, I had no relation to this report, and I do affirm that Mr. Lubin went -- I went from center Beli Manastir to meet that parliamentarians. He was not with me. He went to -- to meet all kind of people around with the sector commander. We are not always -- but we co-ordinated at large. I mean, I -- this is not something that I can say done behind my back, I was something in the dark, no. It's true. But you're busy with your meeting. You come to report on your meeting. You are exhausted with your meeting, and the other one has own meeting, and we, next morning, normally before we start the day, would strategize for the day and regardless of the details of the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Given your experience in the ten days that you were working with Mr. Lubin in Sector East, in his role as the chief of civil affairs, wouldn't he seek out and try to communicate with those whom he perceived to be the most senior interlocutors that he could?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it's not very likely that he would have addressed, would you agree with me, a letter to someone other than the most senior interlocutor he had spoken to; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05933, please, and this is P1390.1351. It's Defence tab 79. If we can turn to page -- if we can just look at the front page, sir, to familiarize yourself. This is a sitrep --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: 22nd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The 22nd of April, 1992, from Lubin to Thornberry --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we can now turn the page. If we go about two thirds of the way down there's a sentence that begins: "My rather long and detailed answer covered our numerous appeals to several" -- something "auth. To control these expulsions, the monitoring mechanism agreement adhered to in principle but not in fact by the Erdut local government. The letter of protest to [sic] Jovic, my letter to Erdut president Dr. Hadzic" -- and it goes on? Again we see here, do we not, a reference to Dr. Hadzic, correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume you ask him about those things and he answer you. I have no knowledge of -- of -- those report I have no control on and what Mr. Lubin was saying. I committed in this court to say the truth, but the truth, and only the truth, and my meeting were the two, twice with Mr. Hadzic who is present in this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason why either you or Mr. Lubin could have been confused about the person, the identity of the person they were speaking to?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't want me to do some speculation here. You want me to the truth --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: To be clear, I'm not asking for speculation. What I am asking is whether there was something in the circumstances of your meetings that could have given rise to that confusion. That's my question.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that there's a mixture here, on -- on mixing things with Mr. Lubin. And I think that Mr. Lubin mixed between Dr. Hadzic and Mr. Hadzic somehow. Maybe -- maybe because the ranking. The fact that he want to communicate with high-ranking locals. I cannot definitely give you a convincing answer, not that I'm going around to deny the answer. I can't. I honestly cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So there's nothing in the circumstances that gave rise to confusion, miscommunication? There's nothing you can think of that gave rise to those elements in any contacts you were having with the local Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One thing I can tell you. Coming from New York or other culture, extremely difficult with those names, extremely difficult to remember those names and exactly even to write them. It took me a while to consider the J as Ye and S with Hat as Sh and C -- this is -- this is something really you had to learn and a long process, difficult. And my handwriting also more difficult. The confusion with the names at the beginning, I would say, it was I think an honest and naive mistake. But later on, if it was something like a few months later I would doubt -- not doubt the intention but the beginning was totally confuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As your superior, did Mr. Lubin do most or all of the talking at the meeting that you attended with Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you say anything at all?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I described things that I -- I seen. Of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But for the most part, you were listening; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: With high-ranking, normally, and I was trained as a bureaucrat in New York you let the superior talk. But in those circumstances I talked, I spoke. In the boat even I spoke. Not -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: During those 45 minutes -- and let's put it a different way: In a meeting of 45 minutes' duration in which Mr. Lubin or someone other person is speaking on behalf of UNPROFOR, wouldn't it be normal for you to take a note of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told not to take notes. In the boat and elsewhere. We were careful. We don't want to be seen as taking notes in the boat was clearly JNA ask us not to take notes. And we took it as a pattern. Regrettably. But this is ... Later on, I did -- we did establish with -- with -- with -- in Bosnia, we established forcibly that we would take notes. But at the beginning, with JNA, in that area, during my time on that area, notes were not being taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So no notes with the JNA. But did you take notes of conversations that you had with local officials?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you make such notes immediately after the meetings?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I use the word plural because I want to be clear: I'm asking you about meetings in general with local civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to come back to the headquarter and to report verbally. And then the evening sitting and write the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you did do that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In reporting, of course. The sitrep was a reflecting what we were -- what we were writing or summary of the meetings. I took some notes for myself in my book later on. I took in Arabic some feelings, some reflections, I had names, recollections, but certainly during meeting, we were not taking notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you had an English-language notebook as well. Were you keeping that English-language notebook contemporaneously? Every day were you recording the events that took place during that day?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily every day. For instance, when we came back from that incident on the 20th, Marinci, I was so hurt I could not sit and write.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We'll come to that even in more detail but -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I know, but I -- and this is for example. And other element, sir, when you come back late, meaning dark time, there is no way you can write the notes. Only next morning, if you have time and not rushing to another incident to write note. Because dark, no electricity, cold, and you cannot write. I wrote some few things. Name -- I tried to write the names in order not to forget those people. But not really serious notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please have 03110, which is Defence tab 286.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is your notebook --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- coming up. And if we could please go to page 12. Now, sir, there, at the top of the page --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You seem to have identified the participants in a meeting. And you say CP Vukovar, his deputy, CP Osijek, head of police department, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. This is the Croats. That's a meeting with the civil police and internal ministry of the Croats in -- of -- of Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So on the 14th of April, 1992, you're taking a note of a conversation with some Croatian officials?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And where does that meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you record the names of those individuals who are participating, correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did -- I did on the top. I'm trying to, yes, I think -- I was taken by Mr. Zitterman, the civil police --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, we don't need to go into a lot of detail.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I just want to have you confirm that, indeed, you did take a note of the individuals participating and the content of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that is during the meeting. That is -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is why the names, I re-correct the names, because we confirm was this the guy, that guy, the names, and the one, two, three, four, I believe I wrote it down after we came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to page 19, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beli Manastir, yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, we're not going to linger on this page because you've distinguished between meetings that you had with UNPROFOR and meetings that you had with local officials, but it does appear to indicate a note of a meeting with Lieutenant-Colonel Joachim. Now then if we turn the page to 21. At the top of the page, it's written: "B Manastir, 17 April, 1992. Meeting with military and civil --"

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civil police. CIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does it say AUT, authorities?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meeting, military, civ ... yeah. Military and civil affairs, yeah. And civil police I think, or affairs. Oh, meeting between Joachim and military and civil affairs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You don't think that there are any local Serb officials present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not in this meeting. This is the guide-lines that wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And maybe, there...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do the questions posed there at the bottom of the page posed, in your view, or in the second half of the page, are they being posed by UN officials or are they being posed by Serb officials?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are our own questions and answers. The team. Those guide-lines with the Lubins.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you realise that there is no notation of any of your two meetings with Mr. Hadzic in your notebook?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if Mr. Hadzic is the man of importance that you believe him to have been, why wouldn't you at least have taken a note of that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- because this was so important that Mr. Lubin has to report it to Mr. Cedric Thornberry. There is no sense of writing two notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you looked at the sitreps that he prepared for Mr. Thornberry on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe yes; maybe no. I cannot specifically, honestly telling you that that report on the meeting of Hadzic, I see that. I really honestly cannot tell you that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You don't recall having looked at those reports and had it jump out at you that the person identified in the reports, as far as you're concerned, is the different from the person you were meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my report because that -- this report was 21st. I already left 21st. The Lubin sitrep, the first, was 21st. I was not there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's look at one reference to Hadzic that does appear in your notebook. If we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, can you read for us that paragraph below the line.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Martic, Martic anti-terrorist police/Erdut, he is the man who given orders to the police with red parade. Practically they are militias. Martic is the boss of Hadzic." It's what I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Where did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either from our sources, civil police, or from the UNMOs. But those are -- something from internal information. Is not from people outside the UNPROFOR personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Otherwise I would mention that I will -- earlier I mentioned that civil -- the police told us that Hadzic this and this, but this, no. This is a note for info.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: On page 20 -- I'm sorry, on page 24, which is the next page of your diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is the -- these are the events of 20th of April and we're just going to look at this briefly. We're going to come back to those events.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But since we have the diary in front of us, it's timely to bring it up. You describe here hearing or being told that there was going to be a removal, transportation of some Croats who want to leave the area. And it says there: "Contact was made with local civil authority and we proceeded together with chief police Vukovar to the village." Now do I understand correctly that your testimony is that you met Mr. Hadzic on that occasion and that that's who you refer to when you say "local civil authority"?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not local civil authority. But this -- we did meet. We had to proceed to that place but through a meeting with Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you saying that when you wrote down "local civil authority," you didn't intend to refer to Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You didn't consider Mr. Hadzic to be what you would describe as a local civil authority, did you?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So why do you think would you have noted that the person you met prior to going to Marinci was local civil authority?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a description between what's written here and what I'm testifying, sir. I'm testifying that we went after we were informed to Mr. Hadzic and then we proceeded to this civil authorities, including the civil police in -- in -- in Vukovar and the mayor of or the head of Marinci.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry. When you say there is a description between, do you intend so say that there is a discrepancy between --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Discrepancy is all right. Okay. And not -- not -- not necessarily negating.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And after you left Sector East and you went to Zagreb and then Sarajevo, did you hear a lot about Mr. Goran Hadzic? Did you hear his name mentioned frequently?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I participated every morning in Sarajevo with Chief of Staff briefing. They have two meetings at the higher level headquarter. It was then the headquarter of UNPROFOR. They first meet with the sector commander and CT, Thornberry, and Chief of Staff, and they have then next meeting organised by Chief of Staff. With this meeting, a briefing from each sector will be presented --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just to cut this short, were the -- did the Sector East reports and presentations mention --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- Mr. Hadzic, Goran Hadzic's name frequently?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that frequently, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you see his photograph --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- then while you were stationed either -- when you were either travelling through Zagreb or stationed in Zagreb or stationed in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You never saw his photograph?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You never saw him on television?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had no television in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And between 1992 and 1995 --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- did you see him on television and hear his name being mentioned frequently?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the mission on April 1993. Went back to New York. And initially I was helping the -- peacekeeping department on the situation in Bosnia. Not in Croatia. So the whole activity, my activity when I came from -- to New York was mostly concentrating on Bosnia, not on Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in that context you never heard anything about Goran Hadzic or saw his photographs or saw him on video?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who was your interpreter when you met Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A gentleman from Beli Manastir. I wrote initially his name and it's in a note somewhere. Maybe here, also the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you consider him to be a reliable interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No indication that he was not translating in a correct and accurate fashion?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not my -- our impression. I trusted him and I thought that he is doing a good job.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will move on to a new topic. It might be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Abd El Razek, this is the time for our second break. 30 minutes again. We will come back at 12.45. You will be escorted out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to apologise if I violated the guide-lines. I did not intend to do so, or do so wittingly. But I do apologise for doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Two things. Firstly, I have to apologise personally for the late start of this third session. I'm the one to blame. I just forgot the time. Secondly, Mr. Abd El Razek, I heard you had some back problems. If there is anything we can do to accommodate you, you -- you need to stand for a moment, or you need a break, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your concern. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gosnell, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, I just want to look a little bit further at your diary or at your notebook, and what we're going to do is look at three different pages and then I'm going to ask you a question at the end of these three pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So if we could, first of all, turn to page 7 of the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, here we have three individuals identified. A Mr. Sablakovic, and Mr. Milan somebody. Can you help us with what you may have written there, after Milan?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: VP of the local government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just below the name Milan, can you --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I think this was the parliamentary. Vice-president of the local government, I believe, is -- would be -- and then Slobodan is the -- the interpreter. Latas was the president of the parliament. Those I met in Beli Manastir. I wrote in Arabic this is a -- the man, middle-aged, Milan, and I wrote on Latas old man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just below the name Milan, there are four letters --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Voij is the family name. Voij something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do I understand you there to be noting that he is the vice-president of the local government of Beli Manastir?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's turn now to page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there at the top, do I understand that you're identifying those individuals as being -- what does CP refer to?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civil police, Vukovar. His deputy, Josef Ranc [phoen], CIVPOL probably. CIVPOL probably is the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're identifying civil police and the head of the police department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that. Yes. Those are the -- the Croatian guys that we met in, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then if we could turn now to page 26, please. Now, here we have an indication of Vujovic's position as secretary of people defence of Vukovar; Dragan Lazic, chief of police; Milan Bentic, head of village?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, those are all indications or instances where you were able to make a notation -- identify and make a notation of the positions of various officials either on the Serbian or the Croat side; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying hard. It's not always easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Don't you think that if you had met the president of the RSK you would have noted that and you would have noted his position?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think I did. Not -- not necessarily in the book. I -- honestly, I don't have an answer, an honest answer for you. Those are the things that I did. Things I did not do at that time, they have their own explanation, not today, I cannot explain it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your testimony is that you went to Beli Manastir three times; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's take a look at some entries in your diary about that. Could we go to page 5. And this, out of an abundance of caution, shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, to be entirely fair to you, at the top of the page you've got a notation, Erdut, and then you've got a notation a little further down, 12 April, 5.45. There's a name which I won't utter because it could be someone who has a particular status, and it says: "Regarding the" something "in the Beli Manastir." Can you tell us what that says without mentioning the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we're going to -- Mr. President, I tried to avoid that. I think we have to redact that reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see, Mr. Gosnell. I think it will be best to remind the witness the precise question, Mr. Gosnell. You asked what the word is after "regarding the," right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Line under -- under the date 12th April.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you see that Mr. Abd El Razek, there's that line. It says Mr. Someone, we won't mention the name, regarding, and then what does it say?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The families in Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, it says: "He is willing to meet the families, cross the bridge in Batina." Now does this in any way refresh your memory that you -- well, were you in Beli Manastir at this time?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this note with Bernard was in our office in Erdut, not on the spot in Beli Manastir. We were communicating with them, and they were, quote up quote, and excuse me for the expression, fleeing the area. They felt as representatives of the Europeans are not wanted in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let turn, if we can, to the next page which seems to have some notations in respect of the 13th of April, and then it says right under that first reference to 13, 4, 1992, it says a contact was made with Mr. -- and we won't mention his name, Mr. Abd El Razek. Now do you recall looking at these notations, were you in Beli Manastir on the 13th of April?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written down. I omitted the EC representative. I went to feed the families to the families in Hungarian in one date. It has to there. It was May [indiscernible]. I think it was the date after that. We met them on the bridge. I think it's the day after or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do you recall where you met these EC officials who you say are based in Osijek?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I met in Erdut. The 13th of -- and April, yes [indiscernible]. Okay. I think that in -- Beli Manastir, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying you did not meet them anywhere in Baranja. You met in Erdut. Is that --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, please. Here we have the page we saw before. It's referring to three -- well, actually, five officials.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Or four officials of Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you got that information when you were in Beli Manastir or did you get that information when you were in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My description in Arabic indicated I did that on the spot in Beli Manastir because I -- I am describing the two men, and one is middle-aged and one old aged. If I wrote it later on, it's a different story. Maybe yes. But I could not write the description of those people without seeing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how long did it take to you travel from Erdut to Beli Manastir by car?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maximum 40. Minutes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 12. We have your meeting with the Croatian officials. Where did that occur?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: With that -- and -- they could not come to the territories, Osijek. Small office in, I think, the headquarters of the police or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you drive directly from Erdut or did you have to pass through Serbia before going to --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had the crossing, with mine land or land-mined cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you recall whether on that day, accepting that there is a crossing, do you recall whether on that day you travelled directly or did you travel through Beli Manastir to Osijek?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It is no sense going to -- through Beli Manastir to Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How long were you in Osijek that day?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent the morning and we were taken to lunch, and then we left back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what time did you arrive back?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not late. Something like 2.30, 3.00, or ... must be not later than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Page 15. This page refers to cases of protection. And on this page there is a reference to Branjina and Jagodnjak. These are both towns in Baranja region, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you are saying what you know. I don't recall this ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, do you recall that on the 15th you were in the Baranja region?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm writing about -- no. I didn't say I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not saying you said you were there. Let me be very clear in my question: I'm asking you whether when you look at this page and you see the information that's written down there, that you wrote down --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- does that remind you that you received this information when you were in the -- that you were on the spot in Beli Manastir or in the Baranja region?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those are -- must be cases that I wrote down in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how would that information have -- how would that information have come to you in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either civil police, mostly civil police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying they drove down and provided you with this information?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were stationed in Erdut. They were travelling -- our civil police, CIVPOL, going up to -- to Beli Manastir, come with information. They'll also I have to recall, information coming us -- coming to us from the European [indiscernible] in from the CRC, the Red Cross. Where is the resource of this information right now? Honestly, I cannot -- [indiscernible] local police [indiscernible] still the same, no. I cannot tell you where it is, but definitely our information came from our resources, not from the local resource.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's look at the next -- the notation for the next day. On page 20, please. 16th April: "Our presence helped protected them," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were you in Beli Manastir or Baranja that day?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16. On the bridge, yes. 16: "Today we worked to facilitate the crossing of the two familiars from the" -- yes, through the Baranja bridge. The ICRC was delayed for two hours, et cetera, et cetera. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How long were new Baranja region on that day?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived earlier. The whole thing took maybe three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Page 21. Next page. Top. It says: "Beli Manastir, 17 April, 1992. Meeting with" -- and we've already discussed that notation. How long were you in Beli Manastir that day?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's not -- it's three, four hours. Not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've said that the meeting you had with Mr. Hadzic occurred some four days before the 20th.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let me just finish my question, please, for the assistance of the transcriber. And that would make it the 16th or the 17th of April, approximately. Can you help us with reference to the notations in your notebook as to which of those days it was --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- that you met with Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be the 18th. I -- I said, honestly, I said, few days before the 20th. Now between the 14th and the 19th, this will be taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you -- you can't situate that meeting --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- with Mr. Hadzic in relation to any of the events that we've just been looking at in your diary?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I was asked before whereby in the [indiscernible]. I failed to give him exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Aren't the vast majority of the entries in your notebook concerning events in Baranja region?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Baranja?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Baranja, my experience, would go to major events. The meeting with the parliamentarians, discussion, concerning the situation, and it would be the -- escorting the two families. Yes. Of course, we had a meeting between and after and before with Mr. -- Colonel Joachim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I put it to you that there's no reference in your notebook to several - let me please finish my question - to several important noteworthy events of civilians leaving the area of Erdut? In fact, isn't it right that there isn't a single reference other than Marinci, the Marinci event, to any transportation of the civilians from the area south of Erdut? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that I did not witness those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. The question was: Isn't it correct that your notebook contains no notation at all of any of those events around Erdut between the 11th of April, 1992, and the 20th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except I have, on the 11, or reporting on the 11 or the 12th, we had report on the three, four incidents between the 8th, 9th -- 7, 8th, 9th, something, on -- on -- on deportation from Erdut, from Dalj, and from other places. But yesterday I failed to pronounce the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, Mr. Abd El Razek, to be clear, and to give you an opportunity to respond, is that looking through your notebook, virtually every notation is about events in Baranja between the 12th and the 20th. My question for you is: Why, if you were based in Erdut during that time-period, wouldn't there be notations about events around the area of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we have on the horses and the two families that came to complain to us. I mentioned somewhere that came to complain and we discuss it with the local police, and the local police said, insisted that they had no charge of those people. As a matter of fact, the local police who served the people who referred us to Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, I put it to you that you were not based in Erdut for most of the time that you were in Sector East, and I put it to you that you never met with Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in this Court, I committed since day one, I am still committed to tell the truth, only truth, and but the truth. I never left on those ten days Erdut. I served in Erdut those ten days. My last day was the incidents of Marinci. I have photos, if you wish, me in the -- in the headquarter. This could be verified. There is the sitreps of -- that mentioned my involvement in -- in the Marinci. I do not have photos of every steps that I walked on that village, but I here to say the truth, to tell the truth, as what I reported, I witnessed here, this is what I know and believe and convey to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you've also told us that your memory of dates and names may be less than perfect. So I want to ask you: Is there any possibility that you have muddled who it was you met and with whom you met them?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe confusing names, but I definitely not confusing the vision, the faces and the people. I never confuse me seeing and meeting with Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You didn't forget the face. How was it that you put the name to the face.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went to meet Mr. Hadzic, we were told that we're going to meet Mr. Hadzic. And we enter his office, we greet him as Mr. Hadzic. Cannot be somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You mentioned that that was an occasion when you were driven by the JNA in a convoy to their headquarters, and I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Gosnell. Could I go back to the answer to your last question. The -- sir, you said that you were told you were going to meet Mr. Hadzic. When you entered the office, you plural, entered the office, you greeted him as Mr. Hadzic. Did he confirm that that's who he was, or did anybody else in the room identify him after you entered as Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, when you shake hands, say, Mr. Hadzic, I thought there is no need for him to say, Yes, I am Hadzic. He did not. But it was clear and we introduce ourselves personally and our duties to Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sorry. Thank you, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You drove in a convoy and I believe that you said that this was during the curfew at night-time. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did not drove through the convoy. We were escorted, our cars were escorted through the camp, forest, into the boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you first of all just tell us how long that drive was, approximately.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maximum 20 minutes to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you have to pass through any gates or sentries or roadblocks when where you were originating and where you ended up?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that we were stopped before the camp itself but we were stopped in the entry of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember that when you crossed the bridge towards Bogojevo, that is the bridge at Erdut, was there a JNA check-point there?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not when we were up -- had the appointment with -- we never been stopped. We stopped other occasions along the road to Dalj or Osijek. But we --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just to clarify my question. I'm referring to when you would pass from Serbia into Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: At Erdut. Did you pass through a JNA check-point on either side of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no bridge from Erdut to Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I was referring to the bridge between Erdut and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. Of course, of course. Eastward. Yeah, yeah, yes. Yes. The term [indiscernible] was yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, sorry, I'm not sure I got your answer. Were there JNA check-points on either side of that bridge?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I think? There was check-points. Whether, it's good question whether it's JNA or -- on that bridge crossing to Serbia, I believe it was either JNA, most probably yes, or police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And can you describe for us, please, the -- what you witnessed, what you observed during this occasion which I imagine was one of the few occasions when you were out at night during the curfew. Well, first of all, let me confirm that. Is it true that that was one of the first occasions when you were moving around after the -- during the curfew?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning going to the meeting with -- with the boat?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just to be clear, my first question is, is it true that this was perhaps the only occasion when you were moving around in the territory during the curfew which, as we know, was from dusk to dawn?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier in this Court that one of the meeting were in the night, late, and other two meetings were in between the day and night. We -- not totally dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's -- let's be clear here. I'm talking about your testimony when you said you drove in cars that had their lights out and you went and visited the JNA boat?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Is that the only occasion when you were driving around or when you were moving around in the territory during your ten days in Sector East, at night-time.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
