utterances.text: The first meeting was really late, in the dark. Other two meetings were something like between 7.00 to 8.00, and initially it was not so dark, but we -- we moved three times. One time through really the curfew and the blackout.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just about those second and third times, did you perceive that the curfew was in effect when you travelled on those two occasions between 7.00 and 8.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we make appointment with the general, and we are escorting to the general, there is no curfew. We are not restricted. We are escorted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I fully understand that, sir. I'm just trying to understand whether on the second and third occasion, you were escorted by - am I correct? - JNA vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Approaching the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was the reason that they escorted you because otherwise you were prohibited to move around at that time?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In entering the camp, was by, itself, restricted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But I'm not now referring to inside the camp. I'm referring from your journey from wherever you originated from, whether it's UNPROFOR Sector East headquarters or whether it was your house, did you have an escort in the JNA for the -- that interval of your journey?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the middle of the village, not from our headquarters. JNA did not risk approach our -- would be escorted on the way to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So between 7.00 and 8.00 p.m., is it your testimony that between 7.00 and 8.00 p.m. you were not required on those two occasions in any event to have an escort?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I did not say that we are not required to have an escort. The escort took place anyway in the camp, approaching the camp, in the camp, anyway, on the three occasions. But in the dark area, was more necessarily to be escorted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let me just put it this way. Did you think there was -- the curfew was in effect when you travelled on the second and third occasions to the JNA camp?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's -- it's -- it's still early in the evening, and I -- I -- I think that we could -- we could manage with -- somehow manage. I mean, I -- this should be a question addressed to the sector commander in the civil police who took care of those businesses. I was taken to meet. I was not arranging the escorting and transportation and logistic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on the second occasion, or excuse me, on the first occasion, that was late at night --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- is it -- was it the case that the streets were deserted?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No people walking, no cars travelling.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I know -- I remember that it's curfew time. Of course, there is the militia is moving there. Police moving there. But not much -- you know, if you drove, you walked through Ilidza -- through Erdut, sorry. Even day-time, you don't see much people, and then we did not see much people around the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Didn't the police tell you that they were also prohibited from moving around during the curfew?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning the local police?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Correct, the local police.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, yesterday during your testimony, you said at 6473: "And we never verified clearly who's enforcing but that the civil police deny any access or any control over this or anything to do with this." That's what you said yesterday --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I [indiscernible]. I insist on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you confirm that the police did tell you that they were prohibited from moving around during the curfew?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on those words. They told me we have no access, we cannot control those people, and they cannot be on -- on the places where those people acting, whether it is because they are ordered not to be there or because the curfew or because other reasons. I did not mention the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean when you say that they told you that they had no access. Didn't you understand that to mean that they considered that they were prohibited from moving around during the curfew?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And other than the three occasions when you travelled back and forth to the JNA camp, was there any other occasion when you were moving around when the curfew was in effect?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did any of your colleagues, according to what you heard, ever try to evade the curfew? Did they ever go out at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there's no where to go out in that night. But, secondly, I don't recall that my colleague, at least Lubins, left their apartments during the curfew. I know that Mr. Zitterman, civil police, lived down the street beyond our areas, and I have no idea whether he was able to move or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you hear any official of the JNA describing the curfew? Anything at all about the curfew?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We complained. No answer. We complain. We said, This is not right, to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did those officials confirm to you that there was a curfew in effect?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: JNA, at large, try to deny any policy or activities or practices on that issue. Say we're outside. This is to the local authorities [indiscernible] either police authorities and the local authorities made those arrangements. JNA denied that has any -- anything to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you saying that they denied there was a curfew that they had declared?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that. I said they had nothing to do with whatever is happening in that territory, night or day-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you hear or see any instances of the JNA present at night-time controlling the roads? And, of course, in this case you will have to rely on those three occasions that you describe that you were out at night.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between our place to the entro at the camp, we see no JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's a very short distance, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All within the outskirts of Erdut, isn't it, both where you were originating from and the camp?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camp is closer to -- what they call it -- Dalj. Down the road on the way to Osijek but the east side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And most of the intimidation and terrorisation of Croat civilians was taking place at night, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably. For instance, in -- in the bridge, Beli Manastir, I saw the bullying those families, day-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure why you need to rely on probabilities. Isn't it the case, from what you know, that most of the harassment and intimidation was going on at night-time?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I wrote and testified that this is the case, but you ask me if I have seen in the day-time. I did decide Marinci. I said on the bridge of Beli Manastir I saw militia pushing those families, dominating them during day-time, not night-time. Most of the reports that we have, we have on raids at night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's why Croat civilians and individuals were so terrified, isn't that correct, because of these acts of intimidation and terrorisation that occurred at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how we were told by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: They told you that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And is it your view that the JNA was co-operating with those who were engaging in those acts of night-time terrorisation and intimidation?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As eye-witness I did not see that -- see that night-time or day-time. Except for Marinci, the tank that was roaming around while the people were deporting the Croats, and then to our surprise to see the general coming to the spot where they left the buses. We were extremely surprised because JNA did claim that they had nothing to do with it. But I confronted him with the tank and he said he will investigate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me -- sorry. Just before this leaves the screen, at page 88, line 21, the sentence in the middle says: "I did decide Marinci..." And I'm not sure if the word -- if the verb "decide" is correct. Maybe you can have that clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you see there on the screen what my learned friend was referring to? Perhaps you can tell us what you said?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before the [indiscernible], that is not -- the statement in the middle says I did decide? What do you mean I did decide Marinci?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's just move on and say that it's a question mark for the transcript. Am I right, Mr. Abd El Razek that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Unless the Prosecution insists on ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, since we're dealing with -- I mean, it's fresh right now. Maybe you want to pose a question to -- just on that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'll try. I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I know what the witness said but I don't want to say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I didn't hear it so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But Mr. Abd El Razek, you see the context in the transcript there. Can you tell what you think you may have said when you were referring to Marinci?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said about the tank that we saw the tank roaming around when -- particularly when after the ambulance brought those two ladies and then we saw the JNA tank with the soldiers on top of the tank and then we -- I complained to the general and referred to these things that he said he will investigate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The people from what you heard who were doing the terrorisation and intimidation at night-time, were they well armed, according to what you heard?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot shoot horses without arms. And shooting at the houses, windows, doors, and then if they are the same people or not, I cannot tell, but I saw them during day-time armed to their teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did the police tell you leaving, aside the issue as to whether they were permitted to go out in the curfew, did the police tell you that they were afraid to conduct patrols at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said two things: (a), they had no control over those; and (b), not afraid but they are -- they preferred not to deal with them. They cannot deal with them. They are not authorised to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's look at your statement, 02789; Prosecution tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could please go to paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "I could distinguish between the police and the militia by the way they were -- they dressed and their behaviour. The police was properly uniformed, professional, organised, and relatively disciplined, but the militia was disorganised, undisciplined, chaotic, not professional, wearing different kinds or mixes of uniforms. I recall the regular police did not like the militia and did not want to be associated with them." Is that all correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the police under the terms of the Vance Plan were only permitted to carry side-arms; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is beyond my testimony. I cannot -- I don't recall that I had this specific provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05928, please, which is P1385.1351. It's Defence tab 74.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is a situation report, Mr. Abd El Razek, coming up on the screen, from Mr. Lubin to Mr. Thornberry.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And point 1 says: "Sector East HQ has received several reports of civilian population expulsions during last night." Is it correct that there were expulsions that actually occurred at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Mostly at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me make sure that I'm clear -- we're clear on the word "expulsion." Do you think that people were moved out at night or that the -- merely the intimidation occurred at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both, sir. There was intimidation during night-time, shooting, and there were also -- that I did not witness. Also, we -- our reports that we had that they were expelled at night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Down at the bottom: "Under existing circumstances, situation cannot be controlled by UNPROFOR. Expulsions are during darkness." Let me first ask you and if you can't answer this question, that's completely fine, do you understand that -- whether UNPROFOR's view at this time was that they should and were entitled to undertake patrols and to control the territory even at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, let me just finish my question. That they were entitled to do that but that they simple didn't have the forces available to do it at that time.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official explanation of our behaviour, our -- our failure to protect the civilians in those regions was officially the lack of deployment, the lack of forces, lack of manpower, lack of contingencies, they can do. However, we also complained that in our headquarter particularly, we are -- we cannot move but that does not mean -- I mean, if we were allowed to move, then we have the contingency to do it. We have only seven soldiers or military personnel, or nine -- seven to nine in the headquarter. Civil police we have two, three in -- in Ilidza too, and in Dalj we have seven people or something like this. No matter what we decide wether it is -- we are permitted or not, we could not handle the situation. I think that major claim of lack of deployment was physically a factualised right, but I have my own reservation on our own position, the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It says: "JNA is not controlling situation and local police do not make night patrols."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that the way it was at the time?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civil police told us they are not going after those guys. Not on those words, no patrol. You know, maybe this is Lubin concept of -- the police told us that we cannot chase, cannot deal with those, cannot go to them, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did the local police seek your assistance in terms of restoring order in Sector East?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say that. I would not say that they seek our assistance. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, before you go on, sir, your answer is -- well, let me just first of all, can you just answer that yes or no or do you think that you need to give an explanation?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the answer, but I would like to give an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not tell us that they need our help. They will be in troubles. But they handed -- their hands are tied. They cannot do things. And they hinted to us to go to other authorities in order to help in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P1389.1351, please. This again is a situation report from Mr. Lubin on the 21st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Item 3: "The meeting was the warmest yet, much open discussion, offers of help, and no political lectures by them. Our appeal for an early-warning system was well received as was our offer to have RusBat establish presence after dark." Does that remind you that in fact there were police officials who were eager to have assistance, in particular, with providing security at night?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way the sentence says -- makes sense. The way I understand and communicate with the local police, they hinted mostly on their lack of ability to act, that their hands are tied. And the fact that they refer us to other authorities means they hinted, maybe, either we cannot do, or please do. Go and -- other authorities to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You say their hands are tied. Isn't it abundantly clear that they -- given that they were facing armed individuals roving around at night in a JNA-imposed curfew, it's not a question of their hands tied, their hands are tied by someone, they simply are not capable --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- to suppress those acts; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I mean, either -- listen, either they don't want to do or they cannot do. In both cases, they did not do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you can't say which of those two is the case?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hard. Difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you some questions about the militia as you've used the term. And you've described to us how you identified or understood the militia, and you've told us, if I'm stating it correctly, that they were individuals wearing a mix of uniforms, usually khaki, not camouflage, sometimes wearing a beret, and sometimes wearing berets of green or --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Red.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- red colour. Is that a correct summary of how you identified the militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was there anything else that would assist you -- and I should add one more thing which you said, which was that you saw no insignias on their uniforms, correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is there any other way that you were able to identify this group that you identify as the militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot of arms, a lot of arms, hand-grenades, arms, bullets, people are loaded with arms going free in the streets, nobody stopped them. I saw them in -- in -- in -- in their compound, around in the winery. They were not illegitimate -- illegitimate. I mean, seeing them, a force, also the check post coming down, up, they can stop you anywhere, when we came back from -- from -- from the crossing with the general, they almost shot us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that almost every adult male in Sector East possessed the clothing that you've described. I cannot say that. I cannot tell you. If you know better than me, fine. But myself, I do not -- I did not see every adult going around with so much arms around his neck and body and hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's have 1307. Defence tab 142.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is considerably later, Mr. Abd El Razek. This is from October 1992. It's an UNPROFOR weekly situation assessment, military information section. If we go to page 2 at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, which section is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's the HQ UNPROFOR, mil info section.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you enlarge it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: There, at the top of the page: "About 70 per cent of civilian possessed" --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you enlarge it, please, a little bit, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "About 70 per cent" -- well, perhaps we should just turn to the previous passage at the bottom. Now this is a report about Sector East.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The only way to hinder terrorism is the disarmament --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this 4 or 5? 5? Paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Under 5.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "The only way to hinder terrorism is the disarmament and disbandonment of the regional milicija. It has to be followed by disarmament of all civilians and," and then if we can turn the page, "the local milicija which is allowed to carry only side weapons." And this is really the sentence that is important: "About 70 per cent of civilian possess weapons at home." But would you agree that there was a wide -- following the war, conflict, there was a wide distribution of weapons, including rifles amongst the civilian population, correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I to say that as eye-witness, I would say -- I did not say -- I not see a whole civilians going around with arms. If it is the information that was running among our headquarters is the responsibility of the -- the -- the author of this documents to testify. I cannot add to their sitrep, and I believe that they will not -- trying to deceive anybody or trying to lie, but this is not what I witnessed in Erdut and Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did anyone advise you while you were in Sector East or before you arrived about the status of, for example, JNA reservists? Did anyone tell you that there was such a group of armed individuals who would be present in Sector East when you arrived there or who were present when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not JNA. I mean the reserves. I was not inform -- or we were inform, actually, that the JNA is not in charge of that -- that area. If it's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When I use the term "JNA reservists," does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So they are not active soldiers. They are reservists, meaning they are recruited when it's needed. If it's my understanding of the reservist. In -- in the -- the people I saw in the camp, they're soldiers. Whether they were reservists or active duty, this I could not verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that there was still an SFRY-declared state of emergency in the territory of the SFRY during those ten days that you were in Sector East?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that I met with this concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that there would be a group there called the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, I read. Nobody told me. We read with sitreps before that in Belgrade. But I -- nobody said and tell me, This is the information that you need to know. If this is satisfy you, but this is what I -- I did. We read many things. Sitreps, not many things, but some sitreps while in Belgrade. Some of those things were mentioned but I cannot say that I witnessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were you able to distinguish between members of the Territorial Defence and members of what you've described here as the militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the same answer, I presume, would follow for JNA reservists who might be activated into service at a particular time, correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only identify soldiers. I don't know with insignia, with uniforms, whether they were reservists or not, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But what insignia did you distinguish between a JNA soldier and the militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The militia do not have insignia, formal one. They have all kind of things. Insignia no. Police they have and in army they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that according to doctrine and law that all armed forces in a zone of responsibility of the JNA are deemed subordinated to the JNA? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, the whole implementation or the cry for Vance implementation is -- was to deal with this issue and to demilitarise and to recreate cease-fire areas and to get the JNA out those areas. This was the purpose of our stay in that -- of our deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you understand that it was the JNA's responsibility to disarm the people whom you've described here as militia? Did you understand that that was their responsibility under the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And I want to -- if I recall, if I may, one of the things that we were telling the general in the boat that it is his responsibility to stop those guys. And he was saying, We are out of the area. We have no responsibility on those areas. Theoretically, they were still to be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: They weren't out of the area, were they? You still saw a significant number of JNA forces in Sector East; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not significant numbers. They have from time to time, I saw armed -- armed carriers, tanks. I saw them more on the -- crossing the bridge to Osijek and in the camp, and most of the armed people I saw during those ten days around our compound or the way to Baranja were not JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But they were still driving around in APCs correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And tanks?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw once or twice tanks in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in military vehicles of other descriptions; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, command cars, something else, yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who was it who told you that the militia was under Goran Hadzic's control?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the civil police, the local police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who precisely?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the name, but, you know, those are the guy who communicate with us. The guy that he mentioned to us in my testimony that they have no control over those guys. This is the guy who told us that was the guys of Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Where was that policeman from?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him locally. Where he is coming from, I have no idea. I could not verify where he where he is come from, from locally, from internationally, from Belgrade, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That would be the Sector East HQ in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I do see the clock, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, this is the end of the third session. We will have another one at 3.00, from 3.00 to 4.30, so let's consider this as a lunch break. The court usher will escort you out of the court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, how -- how are you progressing? Just to know where we are going.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I very much hope to be done in 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. There's a short oral ruling in -- with regard to the Defence motion to admit Exhibit 1D468 filed on 27th of June pertaining to a video exhibit. Defence has stated in the motion that the Prosecution has affirmed it has objection to the admission of the video. Is that right, Mr. -- you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, no. Just for the record, Mr. Stringer has left the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll deal with it tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, is it possible that the person who told you what Mr. Hadzic was the head of used the word "milicija" to describe what he was the head of?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Milicija, we're talking about those arm -- those civilian armed people who are rushing through the houses, night-time terrorising civilians. He was not talking about police or policija or milicija.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's not possible you made a mistake about that given the fact that yesterday you testified at 6470 that you would refer to the police as policea and I assume you meant policija?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Policija or police, they're not militia. Milicija is different than policija, and milicija is those armed - and we defined it yesterday, I'm willing to redefine it today - those --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, you don't need to redefine it.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But the only issue is is it possible, given that you would have expected the word "policija" to refer to police, that the word "milicija" was used in Serb and that you drew the inference that that meant militia in English. Possibly you made that error. It's just that question.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've described the meeting that you had with Mr. Hadzic, and you testified that there were a lot of people coming and going during the meeting. And that's at page 6476. And then at page 3 of today's transcript you say: "There were armed people around and people come in and out almost continuously, whispering to Mr. Hadzic or to handle paper or doing business." Is that description of the meeting correct, that they were -- these people whom you described as militia coming in and out continuously of the meeting and whispering in Mr. Hadzic's ear?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did, at any time Mr. Lubin say, Why are all these people coming in and out continuously during our meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that we interfered in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And your view is that these people who were coming in and out whispering in Mr. Hadzic's ear, your view is that these were a group that you describe as the militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Most?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who wasn't?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, also civilians coming in and out. But I described the armed people who greeting us in the entry and the corridor was then full of them and then some of them would come in and out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why couldn't the people who, assuming that anyone did come in, why couldn't they just have been Mr. Hadzic's body-guards and not members of this militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be. I -- I cannot -- I -- then those are the people I describe as militia. Could be guard. Could be assistant. Could be acquaintance. I had no any way to verify whether they were and their relation with Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How were the police dressed in Sector East?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like most police. I mean, with uniform, with jackets, insignia. And their hats with insignia. With "police." And there is the sign "police." This is the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What colour uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not totally khaki, not military, but police -- to a blueish, to a blueish. Now I cannot totally remember, but they looked like police and I met later on everywhere in former Yugoslavia police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the people coming in and out of the meeting to whisper in Mr. Hadzic's ear, do I understand you to have said that they were sloppily dressed.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. I said -- when I asked how I describe militia, I said some of them looks like sloppily dressed. I did not define those who came in the office in these descriptions. I saw militia outside, I saw people with a really slumpy way dressed, with a lot of, of course, arms. I don't recall that in the office of Mr. Hadzic we had those loose, slumpy, I don't want to say filthy but not clean clothes. I don't see them in this office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a 45 minute meeting between the president of the RSK UNPROFOR, according to you. Doesn't at some point Mr. Hadzic get quite upset that he is being continuously interrupted by these people coming into the room?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was anyone controlling access to the room who was allowing these people to come in and out?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were escorted into his room. We were escorted in. And I was not in the position to control who is controlling the rest of the people into the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was there a secretary?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in -- in the -- in his office. We were escorted to his office, to his desk. I don't recall seeing secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And yesterday at transcript 6477, you twice referred to the theories of Lombroso.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lombroso.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is what you were trying to say yesterday that they looked like criminals?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What exactly I was saying, I don't want to use the Lombroso pattern of identifying people. I'm against Lombroso. I was in criminology and one of the things that we were and still modern criminology totally against Lombroso, and I wanted to say I don't want to term to be a Lombroso saying this ear and this nose and describe in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But that's what you thought. You don't want to express it but that's what you thought; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said it clearly I don't want to use the feature or the nose or the eyes. It's not right. I look at those people on the eyes. I look at people -- I worked with people later on, with those guys. I never looked at their nose or ears to see if they really fitting the pattern of criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was Mr. Hadzic smoking during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. There was lots of smoke in that building. I don't recall seeing him smoking or not smoking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: From that or the other meeting or from any other information, do you know whether he was a smoker?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no position to see if he smoke or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember during your conversation with the Prosecution in 2012 you told them that you believed that Hadzic smoked cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I said that, but I don't now recall that he smoke. The smoke were everywhere. You cannot escape smoking then in former Yugoslavia. Everywhere you go. I had to stop people smoking in the meeting with the parliamentary. In the parliament I complained, and I stopped complaining even. Terrible smoking. Whether Mr. Hadzic smoke or not, I cannot verify but I remember there was a lot of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just to confirm this, am I correct that all three of you, you, Mr. Lubin, and Mrs. Lubin all entered and departed the meeting together?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I'd like to talk to you about the events at Marinci. And how was it that you first learned that morning on the 20th that there was going to be a population movement? Who came and informed you of that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civil police from Vukovar, I believe it was told maybe his deputy, came to inform us about this willing of people who to reach and he referred to our agreement with Mr. Hadzic that we should come and verify that they are leaving on their own, voluntary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the police wasn't hiding this from you, were they?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not hiding for me that they are leaving forcibly. They were telling us there is group of people who want to leave and they want us to witness that they are leaving voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on many other occasions, the police, various police officers had told you that these acts of intimidation were taking place at night, in particular; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say many occasions. And some occasions. Not many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How many occasions?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall in -- in three cases with the police we either approached them or they approached us -- it was mostly we approached them, complained at them, civil -- our civil police, and they talked to us about those occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do I recall correctly that you said that you met in total the police eight times?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In total, eight times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. During that ten days that were in Sector East.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that I said eight times, the police. I -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How many times did you meet the police during those ten days?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- in our headquarter I recall three times. And then the one in the morning was a brief meeting. It was not a meeting. He was calling us to come and...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now when you first had an opportunity to speak with the Croat civilians who were getting ready to be transported, was it your impression that at that stage, regardless of the reasons, at that stage they were terrified and that they wished to leave?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw in their faces the fear. I saw the panic. I saw the tears. Whether then they were convinced they want to leave or not, not all of them -- one of them that I talked to, spoke to, at the beginning, he was reserve, and then he told me that a night earlier, a night or two, night, I think, three of his people were missing, and he want to leave because he's afraid of his life -- on his life, he want to leave. Then he was saying, Leave us alone. We want to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So they weren't happy about leaving but they felt at that stage, given what had happened, that it was, from their perspective, a necessity?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said happy or unhappy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: They were not happy --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But I'm saying that --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at this stage they want to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I want to try and understand precisely the content of the understanding or agreement that you thought you had as a result of the meeting with Mr. Hadzic. What -- what precisely, if you can enlighten us in detail, was the content of the arrangement?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we argued that those people will be forced to leave. The counterargument is nobody is forced to leave. People are leaving on their own. And when kept -- we kept arguing that we had, people talked to us, we had information from civil police, from UNMO, that people were forced. Then we said okay. We agreed on an order to verify that those people leaving on their own, we come to see the people, and some of them they had forms even that I could not read, that they sign forms that they are leaving voluntarily, that our duty as -- as civil affairs UN to see that they are leaving freely. This is the agreement without provisions or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So part of the arrangement that UNPROFOR wanted was that those being -- those who were leaving sign these forms, indicating that they're doing so voluntarily. If not happily but at least indicating that they're leaving voluntarily; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that we'll see to it that they sign those papers. See to it to verify that they are leaving on their own voluntarily. Whether they sign or not is a different story.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you were looking for such papers; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were shown some papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let me clarify. When I say "looking," you expected such papers to be in existence. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We expected that people tell us they are leaving freely because also the barrier of the language, and it is written in -- in -- in Serbian language, and we did not have the interpretation with us on that -- that village. We wanted to talk to the people and they were not talkable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you considered the existence of papers to be relevant to assessing the voluntariness of their departure; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the signature was not forced.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You see, the reason I'm asking you these questions because today at pages 9 to 10 when you were talking about the loading of the bus and the civilians leaving from Marinci, you said: "We didn't see any papers, any signatures." And then you said: "I told them, the police, this is not what we agreed upon." Now, that passage seems to indicate to me - and you can correct me if I'm wrong - that an agreement had been reached, that anyone leaving is going to sign a paper, and that you're going to have an opportunity to check it.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that -- is that the substance of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The substance of the agreement that we verified that they're leaving of their own. The signature should be indicating that they are freely signed that things. There is no way we can in advance say the signature will cover all aspect of this freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that for a moment, sir. But what I am saying is that it appears, at least in respect of Marinci, that you were looking for those documents as an indication. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes. I mean, we looking for any verification that those guys were leaving freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the reason that I find that significant is that you've already told us that you, having spoken to them --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Spoken to one of the group, you already knew having, spoken to that one person, that they were terrified. Didn't you already know that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want me to be frank and open with you, you come to that place, sir. I'm sorry that I'm addressing him [indiscernible]. You come to this place and you see people shaking, crying, it's not impression that those are people happy, standing there waiting for the limousine to take them to a nice restaurant and music. They were shaking, crying. Miserable. Believe me, my heart went out to them. And whether I -- whether they agreed or not agreed, this is what I saw on the ground, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I don't -- I'm not questioning what you saw and that observation. But what I am asking is that having observed that, you were still interested to see --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Some kind of written form --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- in which they -- which they had signed. Is that correct or do I have the order wrong?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask this gentleman if he has a signed form or not. We discussed with the people who guard those people, told them this, This is not what we agreed on. This is not the agreement. The agreement is orderly to see those people orderly express -whether it's by paper or signature or not, I cannot recall - but express their wish and will to leave on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So am I right that you raised this issue --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- on the absence of forms with the policemen, after you had already spoken to the Croat civilian who wanted to leave?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this is the order but definitely when we talked to the police about the mess or the violation of the agreement, we told them we agreed that those people will express, whether it's signing -- or express for me was the express their wish to leave freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You see, the reason why I'm asking you about the sequence of events, I do understand what you're trying to express, but at the transcript today at page 8 at the end you do describe your conversation with the one Croat individual who told you ultimately that he did wish to leave.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then you describe going to the bus with the others. And then it appears from your description that it was at the bus that you raise the issue of the absence of forms with the police. Is that the sequence that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never, in the bus, discuss it with those guards because they were not with us in the bus, sir. We discuss it on the ground. Before we left the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I don't say that you were in the bus with them, but what you say is: "I approached a police" --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And let me go back and read the whole passage.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "By then we have --" And this is at page 9: "By then we have a total of 21 people. We didn't see any papers, any signatures, that while -- while sitting back on that small waiting place, I approached a police. I told them, This is not what we agreed upon."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So I just want to ascertain: Is the part that you did not think was being complied with, the aspect that was not being complied with, was it the fact that you didn't have forms signed by the -- by the Croat civilians?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say no. I would say that we, Andersson and myself, we understood immediately the crime and the scene that those guys, sorry, gentlemen and ladies, those people are leaving not on their own, and if it's not on their own, like the gentleman that I talk with, it was fait accompli. It was not something that we could do anything with. And then themselves, I don't believe except for that woman if you read my earlier testimony, she was holding the bed, holding the door, holding this not to leave the house. The ones that were on the ground, we had an impression and through the talk of the -- a gentleman that, at this point, they're going to leave. Whether they signed paper or did not sign paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In respect of those who are intent on leaving but who have been unlawfully intimidated into leaving, was it UNPROFOR's policy and was it your understanding that you should not allow those people to leave?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that again in Bosnia, and I was really told that it is against, if you help the civilian to leave, against the rules of UNHCR, United Nations High Commission for Refugees, I still, I told Mr. Goulding, I sent him reply, I'm telling you here, I'm telling you your majesty, your excellency, there are certain circumstances I learn in my life, better kick out than killed. I help people at certain points crossing out of their areas in order to protect in terms of their life. I don't -- I never regret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now the individual who you saw who was attempting to force an old lady out of her house, you described him as being a civilian in a semi-military uniform at page 9. Why did you describe that person in that way rather than just saying, This was a person who was a part of the militia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To meet your request, sir, to meet your complaint, sir. I don't want to be obsessed with the term "militia." I still don't want to be obsessed with this. I know a civilian who wore semi-uniforms, who arms or has a police belt with -- with -- with arm -- army grenades, with bullets, with machine-guns, with a green or red beret. In this sense, I think it was a green beret -- not -- sorry. Not green beret. I describe him as a person, this description. I have no problem calling him militia, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was this incident occurring within eyesight of the place where the JNA tank was?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The ambulance was -- not this incidents. The tank, later on we drove not far from there. We stop by an ambulance, medical ambulance with two ladies, one of them handicapped. While loading those two ladies, I saw the tank. Not while protecting the woman in the house. The JNA tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, one -- one second, please. Mr. Abd El Razek, you seem to correct yourself about the colour of the -- of the beret. Green, red. Do you know or don't you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say I can swear that it's red or green.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my impression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the policemen with whom you were discussing the issue of the -- at -- where you confronted or came across the ambulance, now what was it that you precisely were suggesting he had not done properly or that -- what aspect of the agreement, in your view, he had not fulfilled?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I correct you, sir? I did not say I saw the police or discussed with the police with ambulance incidents. The only talks with the police were on the sides and that we protested. Once we loaded the bus and drove the bus, there was no police with us. The ambulance is when we start loading the people. Andersson and myself told the guy or the gentleman, the person this is not right, et cetera, et cetera. But while in the bus, and we drove, first of all, followed this gentleman -- or this armed person to push the woman out. There was no police in that section. That section, no. And the ambulance was after the incidents with the woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're saying no police witnessed this event with the --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- with the person wearing semi-military clothing?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except our civil police, of course. Andersson.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I just want to show you two JNA documents. There are others but I won't show you those.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we have 06072, please. This is Defence tab 295.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is a document which I understand from the Prosecution is dated the 13th of January, 1992. At least according to the description that's uploaded. And if we could turn the page -- well, first of all, does that reflect what you recall the layout of the street plan of Marinci to have been?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You got me on this now. We came from Vukovar, we drove through main road, we stop in the office, we go to that road to the end, we saw those people, and we drove back to Osijek. The layout of the village, beyond me, I'm sorry. I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you recall if there was a Territorial Defence headquarters or did anyone say that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We went into that office they called the head of the village office. Not military, not the police office. This was a civilian place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we go to page 4 of the document, please. In English. And I'm interested in item 7 -- well, we can go to page -- yes, item 7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you tell me what date is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: My understanding is it's the 13th of January, 1992. Number 7, Ivo Kelic ran off and joined the ZNG. All his belongings are in the house." Now, sir, I know you haven't seen this document, but you have mentioned that houses were targeted.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Those houses of non-Serbs. Did you ever hear that the JNA had undertaken an inventory or a survey of houses to determine who was Croat and who was Serb?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen document. Somebody was mentioning that. It was not in my main -- main interests or main document or main testimony. I heard that, but I cannot verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And leaving aside ethnicity, did they -- did you hear that they were tracking who had gone and joined the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This only by hearing from others, but not knowing, I have no knowledge serious knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you know that they had taken a comprehensive survey of houses in the settlements where they had town commands?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I -- I think that, you know, those -- one of those documents on one of those issues was raised in Security Council. That I don't recall which meeting of Security Council. That was in the air. But I cannot tell that I myself in those times was -- had any access to these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06179, please, which is P1718. Now, this, sir, is a JNA document dated the 25th of April, and it specifically refers, I think, to the events that you witnessed. And in paragraph 3, and, for the record, this is from Lieutenant-Colonel Miroslav Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Who ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Appears to be from the 1st Mechanized Corps based in Principovac. Paragraph 3 says: "Specific examples were provided of two villages around Vukovar and Marinci village emphasising that this was perpetrated by armed bands and that this was happening regardless of the warning from the head of the UN to Borislav Jovic and their talks with JNA representatives." Now let me just stop there. Why are the protested or the talks regarding this incident taking place with Mr. Jovic and with JNA representatives, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the general showed himself on the crossing area to our all surprise. If he shows himself on the -- on the deportation or expelling area while those people were expelled, regardless of who if he decided or is under control or if he -- the one order it, he is the highest or was the highest rank and the highest one to be responsible for what happens, regardless if his people did that or other people did. Being in the region, the general rank with the buses giving to the Columbian driver to move into Osijek, and prior to that a tank, a JNA tank, how you could overlook their involvement in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And is it also because the JNA had signed the Geneva agreement which was the foundation for the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess so. I mean, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you understand that to be the case, that the JNA was a party with whom you as UNPROFOR had to deal because they were specifically a party to the Geneva agreement and the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any agreement, sir, between countries, peoples, regions, will be the officials -- with whom the officials of those agreement. The UN normally with Geneva Convention and Geneva agreements and all kind of agreements will be UN as the hosting party and the fighting parties will be the parties to the agreement. My understanding then that in the Security Council deliberation, the representative of the former Yugoslavia, the ambassador in UN, was leading the deliberation of those agreements with and through the UN Security Council president. JNA was a major party to those agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says: "They also expressed," and by "they" they're referring to whoever was there on behalf on UNPROFOR, "also expressed amazement and a lack of understanding of how it armed bands could get by JNA centuries and that centuries did not check whether the people were leaving voluntarily." Now this reference to "centuries" I can only assume is a reference to "sentries." Did you provide information up the chain of command in UNPROFOR that there were sentries at Marinci when this displacement was taking place?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you did know that they crossed -- when they crossed into Croatia, they did pass through a JNA check-point; right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, am I right in understanding your testimony that some members of UNPROFOR actually drove the buses across the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How did that occur?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- the Serbian drivers of the buses refused to take the buses to Osijek, Kiseljak knowing that they will be arrested, and somehow - I don't recall and I was not because I was rushing to the headquarter - somebody convinced our UNMOs, our Columbian UN soldiers to drive the buses and they did. I cannot judge it today. I cannot pass judgement on this, but I think it was a mistake to drive them by UN drivers. And I -- I can pledge of those people that I have -- they did it out of respect and trying to help the people, not knowing that they are really not doing well for the agreements and for the entire enterprise of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If UNPROFOR was opposed to their transportation out of the area, shouldn't those Columbians have been ordered not to participate in this?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know by whom, sir. I'm telling you, on the ground, that area we have UNMOs, United Nations Military Observers, and there's the police of Dalj, not all of them there, the people who were on the ground were very low rank, devoted, committed UN soldiers but not knowing exactly. If I were them, then maybe but now definitely I would refuse to do it. But you cannot -- I cannot put myself in their shoes. I cannot judge or pass judgement on them. It was our fault. It was not good for UNPROFOR, not was good for our images, and the Croats made it clear loud on the TV all over, sir, all over Croatia and western Europe, all over was this news that UNPROFOR is helping the ethnic cleansing and Lubin was the first to be then accused. They skipped my name as [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Abd El Razek, bad publicity is one thing. Wasn't it perfectly humane for UNPROFOR in the specific circumstances that you confronted in respect of those individuals at Marinci, wasn't it perfectly humane to assist those people to leave under the circumstances --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- circumstances that were not within UNPROFOR's control and circumstances that are not desirable? But nevertheless under the circumstances, wasn't it a humane and appropriate action to facilitate their departure?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree more with you, sir, and I think -- I think this morning I mentioned that the discussion with Andersson on the spot, we thought we better escorted those people, preserve some of their dignity, integrity to wherever the buses will take us. I'm not sure that this was legally -- not in the sense of the legal implication of the agreement was good, but I never regret this thing. Until today, I'm willing to stand for this action.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P380, please. This is Prosecution tab 28. Now, you testified earlier about the re-painting of certain military equipment to --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- have it appear as police equipment. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one vehicle, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Only one vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on we have more information, but the ones that I saw I saw only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this document in front of us is from the command of the 12th Corps, and the signature -- the signatory is Mr. -- General Biorcevic, and this document appears -- it's dated 27th of April, 1992, so that's after the period that you were in Sector East, and this appears to be the order that is authorising the transfer of military equipment or the re-painting of military equipment. Are you sure that you saw a re-painted vehicle prior to the issuance of this order?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that you have enough experience, sir, to understand the approval or legal approval of a project is not always coming before the production line. But I seen, as I seen, when they legalize it or order it, many things that reordered came back or came later on. Is not the first things that documents and orders cover up for the things that they did earlier. This is my impression. And anyway ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And one final question and it's taking you back to the -- to your -- where you were based in Erdut. You said that there was a wood or a forest nearby. Do you remember that, saying that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forest by where? By the boat? By the boat is not Erdut. It is Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So that's where the forest was?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camp was covered by forest. But in our area where I -- I stayed in Erdut, there were ruins and some trees but not forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I just have one more question for you, sir. When you were in Marinci and you spoke to the group of Croat -- the one Croat individual in the group, were you accompanied by an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how did you manage -- I assume you don't speak --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- Serbian?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Ask the question and the person answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: They responded to you in English?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He answered me in English, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no interpreter then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do you have any idea the name of this person you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Abd El Razek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Abd El Razek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I begin, I sent an e-mail to my learned friend and to the Trial Chamber with respect to a series of four photos which Dr. Abd El Razek gave us a few days ago. Initially I did not intend on using them, however, in light of the answers he gave us this morning, to assist him in identifying the name of the sector commander, I would seek leave to add these photos to assist him again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Did you get a reaction from the Defence, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I did not at this stage, Your Honours. And just to clarify it, I will not seek to tender them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: There's no objection to that Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These photos are at 65 ter 6469. We will look at them a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Dr. Abd El Razek, this morning, my learned friend from the Defence put to you that you were not based in Erdut during the time -- your time in that area. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please look at the following document. It is Exhibit P1384.1351, at tab 15. Now, Dr. Abd El Razek, I'm not interested in the substance itself or the topic but this document is drafted by Mr. Lubin and sent to Mr. Thornberry on the 17th of April, 1992. And it -- it deals with issues in Beli Manastir but this is not what I'm interested in. But I want you to look at paragraph 2. If you look at the eighth line, line number 8 which starts with: "Constant monitoring ..."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "[Indiscernible] therefore Adnan Abd El Razek will accompany..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Can I ask you to read that sentence out loud starting with "therefore"?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... therefore Adnan Abd El Razek will accompany me to -- re meet the local officers preparatory to my location locating him in Beli Manastir by weekend for as long as it takes for situation to calm, realise that we cannot cover sector from headquarter, used some staff will -- with periodically have to stay with battalions to establish UNPROFOR credibility and ease local tensions."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. When he writes "we cannot cover sector from HQ," which HQ is he talking about?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Erdut HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And when he talks about the fact that some staff will periodically have to stay with battalions, which battalions is he referring --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Belgian Battalion there Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And finally when he writes that he will go to meet local officials there, preparatory to my locating him in Beli Manastir, what does this document suggest about where you were stationed until then?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I comment on this? Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If it could assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If necessary, Mr. Abd El Razek, and if relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I highly appreciate this Court. I respect you and your team. I did not want to then reply to the provocation that obviously that I was not that entire testimony -- entire ten days that I went to that region were hoax or I was not there. I too much respect this Court to answer it in my own way. In any case, there's records of the UN staff where they station everywhere, and this Court can order somebody to request the UN to show the records and also where I stayed overnight on this place. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you explained today that in the Erdut headquarters, the battalion commander was -- was stationed there. And yesterday, if I understood you right, you explained that the sector commander would from one of the national contingents present on the ground. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I think I told you Sunday --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yesterday in the courtroom at page 6463.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But prior to that Sunday I noticed that it was said that -- the chief of battalion, and I corrected, it's not the commander of the battalion who was in Erdut but the sector commander, the Belgian sector commander. Now I want to elaborate on. Any headquarters of sectors will contain people who represent mostly the battalions in that sector. The biggest battalion then, and almost I think they are the only battalion, platoon they were battalion -- but battalion, the only battalion was the Belgian Battalion in Beli Manastir, and the chief of the -- the -- the commander, sector commander, the chief of the sector the Belgian chief due to the fact that this battalion was stationed in Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Who -- who was the -- do you remember him by name, the sector commander?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the photo that I -- I took with him in the back of the photo, there's his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
