utterances.text: Can we perhaps display it now. This is 65 ter 6469. Can we go to page 3, please. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Dr. Abd El Razek, what we're looking at here.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The far left, this is the commander. Myself in the middle. And to my left, the far right in that photo, is the Chief of Staff. Both names are behind that photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you help us with where this picture was taken?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the section -- two sections got into the compound. One is the military, all the equipments, and this one here is our building. This is in front of their building. This setting would be typical when we are too cold inside go up a little bit in the sun to warm up before we go back to the -- to the internal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the entry of the military office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can we now go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what are we -- what are we looking at here, Dr. Abd El Razek?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This is Venderwee, Venderwee, sector commander, and then up Strilo -- Strivlink [phoen]. I'm sorry, I'm not good on names, but this was Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And where was this written?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the back of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On the back of the photo. So this is the back of the photograph we were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the back of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So these are the two names that --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for my name on that towards the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can take away the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'll move onto a different topic, Dr. Abd El Razek. This morning you were shown some excerpts from your notebook, if you remember. Just as a curiosity, do you have the original with you here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was yesterday told not to bring it. I mean, that -- my -- my handwriting thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I played good boy and didn't bring it to the court, but I have it in the hotel. Ironically, I am --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine. We'll try to do with the version we have in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we pull up 65 ter 3110, please. And can we please go to page 5.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the internal cover and external cover is -- is leather.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now at page 5 here you were shown this this morning by my learned friend. This is a note you took with the header: Erdut, 12th of April. Can we now go to page 6. Next page. Now, at the bottom of this page you're recorded on the 13th of April meetings with EC members. Can you see the last sentence at the bottom of your notepad. It says: "The witness occasions when" -- and the sentence --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "They witness occasion" -- well, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- I know what I mean. But, you know, I cannot swear that this is true. But witness occasion when people were deported.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a second. Before you come to any conclusions. If we scroll all the way down you can see that the sentence does not end here. It continues. Is that right? Okay?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So if we go to the next page which you were shown also today, page 7. Here, the sentence does not continue. We see some names --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then another page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. So if we go to the next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to object to the next page. I didn't show the next page, didn't ask anything about the subject matter that's about to be gone into, so it's beyond the scope of the cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What I'm trying to get at, Your Honours, is that there was an inference made during the cross-examination about the names that we see now on page 7, and my learned friend made a relationship between this page and the one we saw before. What I want to show is that page 6 continues on page 8. And what we'd like to get to is what do we see now here, who these names are. That's what I'm trying to get. So I will not get into the subject matter. If that's what my learned friend is worried about, I will not -- and I will stop the witness if we get to that. I'm not interested in the subject matter of the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I have to maintain the objection, regrettably, Mr. President, because what's on page 8 doesn't in my opinion have -- assist in understanding the relationship between page 7 and 6, and in fact my questions concern the relationship between page 7 and both page 6 and 5. And that's the context where you see the connection. I don't think the few words on page 8 are helpful and they're prejudicial. So the objection is maintained, but I'm in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I have a compromise here. I'll try to deal with page 7 without going to page 8. I'll look at -- I'll questions about this, the page that we have in front of us without going to the next, but if it becomes necessary I'll apply again to look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Dr. Abd El Razek, we're looking at this page here with names. Does it follow from the previous page?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not trying to be funny. But when you flip the papers and you have something in your mind you write -- while are you writing a report and you go back and use this page and that page. Remember, this is -- the whole thing is not in -- in a luxury office in Manhattan in the UN building. This is done in a very unorganised place, and we -- apparently I wanted -- the name of those guys, and the telephones. Why they are speaking. I asked the name, I wrote, and then this page was with this. I remember and -- you see that I -- I tried to illuminate this things, and then I had a description of those. I claim that this page should not seen in any way as interrupting the page before and after. This is page -- I could -- unfortunately, I didn't bring with me the things. If you see in the top -- in the first page, something has nothing to do with the immediate meeting when we came to -- to -- to Erdut. Something else. At one point, I had to write it. I wrote. But ... well, it is in the hands of -- of -- of Their Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, just to be perfectly clear, if you are looking at your notebook and you started writing the notes that we saw on the previous page with respect to your meeting with the EC monitors, where does this page appear? The one that we're looking at. Where is it. Is it in the -- if you're looking at your notebook --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Which you don't have here.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know if it's in the immediate page, next page, or where is it?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: With what? With a --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What we're looking at here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go back to the first -- to the one before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I can see where we're going. I have no objection if the Prosecutor wants to show the page after to assist with this line of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm afraid that unfortunately the original would have helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me just put it this way: What we're looking at, this page, is it on the flip side of the previous page or is it on a separate sheet?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the same -- the same paper and I -- this is the same book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I -- you mean if I start -- I start taking the notes or writing the notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No, no, no. Let's go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Demirdjian, it would assist the witness if you to hold up a pad to show him what you mean, a pad that's bound in the way that says -- I follow it, but the witness may have difficulties -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now I have a pad in front of me.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The page that we're looking at --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- would it be on this side or the next on this side, can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, this is what you're asking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And perhaps if we could zoom up on this picture. Can we zoom up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Zoom all the way up, please. All the way up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you see the binding? You see the binding --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The binding in the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The spirals. Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. And this is coming here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, yeah. It's again coming down, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Are you able to assist us? Unfortunately you don't have your notepad. Whether we're looking at -- a page that is on the flip side of what we saw before? Are you able to assist us in any way?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will live with this. Let me move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm too old handle those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Today at page 79 of the transcript you told us there is not a single -- no, sorry, you were asked by my learned friend, it was put to you, in fact, that there is not a single reference in your notebook to any transportation of civilians south of Erdut. And this was a reference to anything like Vukovar, et cetera. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: South of Erdut. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This was the question put to you?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Correct. And then I talked about the north and he corrected me and we went back to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I take you to page 12 which we looked at this morning. This the 14th of April notes you mentioned earlier with respect to a meeting with Croatian authorities in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see under item 2?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Item 2.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 2, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: "The safety of Croatians in the sector (expulsion). 48 Almas." Then after some dates you have Erdut, 84 persons. Right? At the bottom of this page, under item 4, the very last line --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we scroll all the way down.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The very last line. Do you see that sentence that starts with: "500 expelled from Vukovar"? Now just very briefly can you tell the Court how did these discussions come about.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like we being complaining about the practices of -- of -- against the civilians. When we came to -- this is -- came out of the meeting with the civil police of Osijek. They listed their complaints. Those, for instance, if you see 48 Almas, it is 8 of April. I was not there on 8 of April. And this 9 of April. 9 of April on. This information came from that -- from -- in the meeting with those police and internal minister not only police of Osijek. This -- those are not numbers that we verified, [indiscernible] definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This was conveyed to you by whom exactly?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: By those we met, chief of police and deputy or something, internal minister of Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. There are two items from the transcript that I'd like you also to clarify. Today at page 88, you were asked the following question: "Isn't it the case from what you know that most of the harassment and intimidation was going on at night-time?" You answered as follows -- in fact, the beginning of you answer was indiscernible but then the following was recorded: "I have seen in day-time, I did decide Marinci. I said on the bridge of Beli Manastir, I saw militia in day-time not night-time." So, Dr. Abd El Razek, this brings me back to the word "decide." Can you help us here? The sentence was recorded as: "I did decide Marinci."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Makes no sense. I did decide Marinci. Maybe I did so on Marinci. Decide, definitely not. And to be fair with this question, I said I saw on -- on the day-time but most of the things were happening in the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. At page 92, you were talking about the manpower available at the time in the area with respect to the UN. You said the following: "Civil police, we have two, three, in Ilidza too, and in Dalj we have seven people or something like this."

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Ilidza. In Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And the last topic --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said Ilidza and then I said Erdut. Ilidza is that entry on into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just wanted to clarify that. Thank you. Finally, with respect to the last topic, you were asked by my learned friend today about the forms which allege that the Croat individuals left voluntarily. Did you see any of these forms at the time when you were there during the 11 days that you were --

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- based in the [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh yes. I saw forms. But not -- not with those people in Marinci. No, I saw form.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what did these forms say?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, it was not really totally translated, but there's a name, description, and there is something. I saw also the signature. Something saying that we want to leave or a simple question. I cannot right now and today telling you exactly, but I know that there is information about those applicants, and there is date and signature in between. I cannot recall. But something that they agree to leave. I mean, those forms will indicate that those people are voluntarily leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And finally how did you view such document?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN ABD EL RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went to complain that we were [indiscernible] trust those documents before or when are not present to verify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is all I ask. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, I have a clarification question of you before I can put a question to the witness. At 66:8, 9, and further down, it's about the meetings, or the meeting, that the witness said he had together with Mr. Lubin with Mr. Hadzic. And you asked him -- you asked the witness whether he had seen and eventually his attention being drawn to the fact -- whether he had seen the sit-reports made by Mr. Lubin on this occasion and whether he had seen eventually that the Hadzic in the sit-report was not the Hadzic he was talking about. This is at 66:13, 14, and 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, can I confirm it's page 66 of the provisional transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's page 66 on my screen, yes. But it wouldn't be the first time that I almost understood that our -- our numbers are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It does seem to be the same. I see the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now and then you asked to pull up a sit-report of the 21st of April, in which, indeed, it is said that -- that -- where -- where mention is made of Dr. Hadzic. Witness responding that that was after he left the region. Now my question is -- because I tried to locate the sit-reports of -- made by Mr. Lubin on the occasion of the meeting, or meetings, with Mr. Hadzic. I couldn't find them. Could you assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's, I believe, 65 ter 05932.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 65 ter ... Could we have that on the screen, please. Let's see whether we can find the date. 21st of April as well. Now that's -- that's the one -- that's the one you asked for. So the -- there is -- there -- the witness said there were two meetings. One with Mr. Lubin, three or four days before the 20th of April. So I take it then that we don't have a sit-report on -- on that meeting from Mr. Lubin? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I can't answer you with certainty now, Mr. President. Not to my knowledge at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So basically, then, this is the one you based your question on that Mr. Lubin mentioned another Hadzic, namely, Dr. Hadzic; right? That's the one, and that's the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: There's also P1390.1351.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we have that one on the screen, please. So this is from the day after, the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's correct. And there's a reference to Dr. Hadzic on page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And to a meeting with Dr. Hadzic on page 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No. No -- there's no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just mentioning the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. In that case, I have no question for the witness. Mr. Witness, Mr. Abd El Razek, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague to assist us. You are now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I appreciate this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't think there's anything else. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of July, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
